vulnerabilities.title: Injection Vulnerability in Application
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement input validation and sanitization using parameterized queries
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries or ORM for database operations
Implement whitelist-based input validation
Sanitize all user inputs before processing
Use prepared statements for SQL queries
Encode outputs to prevent XSS

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authentication in Application
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement strong authentication mechanism (OAuth, JWT, MFA)
remediation_steps: Implement authentication layer (OAuth 2.0, JWT)
Add authorization checks for all sensitive operations
Implement multi-factor authentication for high-value operations
Use secure session management
Implement rate limiting

vulnerabilities.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Application
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement context-aware output encoding
remediation_steps: Encode all user-controlled data in HTML context
Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers
Implement HTTP-only cookies for sessions
Sanitize HTML using a whitelist approach
Use auto-escaping template engines

vulnerabilities.title: Unencrypted Sensitive Data in Transit: User Requests
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement TLS 1.3 for all sensitive data transmission
remediation_steps: Use TLS 1.3 for all communications
Disable weak cipher suites
Implement certificate pinning
Use HSTS headers
Enforce HTTPS redirects

vulnerabilities.title: Credential Stuffing Attacks
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA), rate limiting on login attempts, and account lockout mechanisms. Use breach password detection (e.g., Have I Been Pwned API) to block compromised passwords.

vulnerabilities.title: Session Hijacking via Predictable Session Tokens
vulnerabilities.fix: Use Flask's built-in session management with secure, random session tokens (e.g., Flask-SeaSurf or Flask-Talisman). Ensure tokens are long, random, and regenerated after login. Use HTTPS to encrypt session data in transit.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) for Account Takeover
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations (e.g., login, password updates, profile changes). Use Flask-WTF or Flask-SeaSurf to enforce CSRF protection.

vulnerabilities.title: Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) Attacks on Login
vulnerabilities.fix: Enforce HTTPS with strong TLS configurations (e.g., TLS 1.2 or higher, HSTS headers). Use Flask-Talisman to enforce secure connections and headers.

vulnerabilities.title: Brute-Force Attacks on Login Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement rate limiting on login attempts (e.g., Flask-Limiter), account lockout after failed attempts, and strong password policies (e.g., minimum length, complexity).

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR) for User Impersonation
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement proper authorization checks for all user-specific requests. Use indirect references (e.g., UUIDs or session-based mappings) instead of exposing direct object references. Enforce role-based access control (RBAC).

vulnerabilities.title: Phishing Attacks for Credential Theft
vulnerabilities.fix: Educate users about phishing risks and implement multi-factor authentication (MFA). Use email verification and domain validation to reduce the risk of fake login pages. Monitor for suspicious login attempts.

vulnerabilities.title: Session Fixation Attacks
vulnerabilities.fix: Regenerate session tokens after login and logout. Use Flask's built-in session management to ensure session tokens are invalidated and regenerated securely.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection in Login and Search Endpoints
vulnerabilities.fix: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements to separate SQL logic from user input. Implement input validation and sanitization for all user-supplied data. Use an ORM (e.g., SQLAlchemy) to abstract database interactions.

vulnerabilities.title: Unauthorized Data Modification via API Endpoints
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement strict access controls to ensure users can only modify their own data. Use CSRF tokens for state-changing operations (e.g., POST, PUT, DELETE). Validate and sanitize all input data on the server side.

vulnerabilities.title: Tampering with Database Files Directly
vulnerabilities.fix: Restrict file system permissions to ensure only authorized processes can access the database file. Store the database in a secure directory and consider using encryption for sensitive data at rest. Regularly audit file permissions and access logs.

vulnerabilities.title: Manipulation of Session Data
vulnerabilities.fix: Use server-side session management or signed tokens (e.g., JWT with strong signatures) to prevent tampering. Ensure tokens are invalidated after logout or expiration. Use HTTPS to encrypt session data in transit.

vulnerabilities.title: Data Tampering via Import/Export Functions
vulnerabilities.fix: Validate and sanitize all imported data. Use strict file format checks and reject files with unexpected content. For exports, ensure data is properly escaped and use secure file transfer methods.

vulnerabilities.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Leading to Data Tampering
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations. Use the `SameSite` attribute for cookies to prevent CSRF attacks. Educate users about the risks of clicking on suspicious links.

vulnerabilities.title: Tampering with Logs to Hide Malicious Activity
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement write-once-read-many (WORM) logging mechanisms to prevent log tampering. Store logs in a secure, centralized location with restricted access. Use digital signatures to ensure log integrity.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing or Insufficient Audit Logs for User Actions
vulnerabilities.fix:
Implement comprehensive audit logging for all critical actions, including:
- User logins (successful and failed attempts)
- Profile modifications (e.g., email, password changes)
- Data imports and exports
- Search queries involving sensitive data
- Administrative actions
Logs should include timestamps, user IDs, IP addresses, and action details. Ensure logs are stored securely and are tamper-evident.

vulnerabilities.title: No Logging of Sensitive Data Access
vulnerabilities.fix:
Log all access to sensitive data, including:
- Who accessed the data
- What data was accessed
- When the access occurred
- The IP address and user agent of the requester
Ensure logs are protected from tampering and reviewed regularly.

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficient Logging of Administrative Actions
vulnerabilities.fix:
Implement detailed logging for all administrative actions, including:
- User role changes
- System configuration modifications
- Database schema or data changes
- Access to administrative endpoints
Logs should include timestamps, user IDs, action details, and IP addresses. Store logs in a secure, tamper-proof system.

vulnerabilities.title: No Logging of Failed Login Attempts
vulnerabilities.fix:
Log all failed login attempts, including:
- Username or email used
- Timestamp
- IP address and user agent
- Reason for failure (e.g., incorrect password, account locked)
Use these logs to detect and respond to brute-force attacks.

vulnerabilities.title: No Transaction Logging for Data Imports and Downloads
vulnerabilities.fix:
Implement transaction logging for all data imports and downloads, including:
- User ID and IP address
- Timestamp
- Type and size of data imported/downloaded
- Source/destination of the data
Store logs securely and ensure they are tamper-evident.

vulnerabilities.title: No Logging of Search Queries Involving Sensitive Data
vulnerabilities.fix:
Log all search queries involving sensitive data, including:
- User ID and IP address
- Timestamp
- Search parameters and results
- Type of data accessed
Ensure logs are reviewed regularly and protected from tampering.

vulnerabilities.title: No Logging of Session Management Activities
vulnerabilities.fix:
Log all session management activities, including:
- Session creation and termination
- Token generation and invalidation
- User ID and IP address
- Timestamp
Store logs securely and review them regularly to detect suspicious activity.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Sensitive Data in Error Messages
vulnerabilities.fix: Disable debug mode in production. Implement custom error pages that do not disclose internal details. Use logging to capture errors for internal review without exposing them to users.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Profile and Search Endpoints
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement proper authorization checks to ensure users can only access their own data. Use indirect references (e.g., session-based mappings) instead of direct object references. Validate and sanitize all user inputs.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection Leading to Data Leakage
vulnerabilities.fix: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements to interact with the database. Implement input validation and sanitization for all user-supplied data. Use ORM frameworks like SQLAlchemy to abstract database interactions.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Sensitive Data in Logs
vulnerabilities.fix: Avoid logging sensitive information such as passwords, session tokens, or PII. Use log redaction or masking for sensitive fields. Implement strict access controls for log files and monitor log access.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure API Responses (Over-Posting)
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement data minimization in API responses. Use serialization libraries to explicitly define which fields are included in responses. Avoid returning sensitive data unless absolutely necessary.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Database Backups or Snapshots
vulnerabilities.fix: Store database files outside the web root directory. Implement strict access controls to prevent unauthorized access. Use environment-specific configurations to secure database storage. Regularly audit backup storage locations.

vulnerabilities.title: Sensitive Data Exposure in URL Parameters
vulnerabilities.fix: Avoid transmitting sensitive data in URL parameters. Use POST requests for sensitive data and ensure tokens or credentials are sent in request headers or bodies. Implement URL rewriting to obscure sensitive parameters.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Internal Network Information via Ping Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Limit the information returned by diagnostic endpoints. Avoid exposing internal hostnames, IP addresses, or network details. Use generic success/failure responses for such endpoints.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Sensitive Data in Download Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement strict authorization checks for the download endpoint. Validate file paths and ensure users can only download files they are permitted to access. Use indirect references (e.g., UUIDs) instead of direct file paths.

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Session Tokens in Import Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Validate and sanitize all imported files. Avoid processing sensitive data in uploaded files. Implement file type and content validation to ensure only expected data is processed.

vulnerabilities.title: SQLite Database Locking Due to Long-Running Transactions
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Replace SQLite with a more scalable database like PostgreSQL or MySQL for production environments. 2. Implement query timeouts to limit the duration of database operations. 3. Use connection pooling to manage database connections efficiently. 4. Optimize queries and batch large operations to minimize lock duration.

vulnerabilities.title: Resource Exhaustion via File Uploads
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Enforce strict file size limits for uploads and downloads. 2. Implement rate limiting on file upload/download endpoints. 3. Use server-side checks to validate file types and sizes before processing. 4. Store large files in a separate storage service (e.g., AWS S3) and serve them asynchronously.

vulnerabilities.title: Ping Endpoint Abuse for Network Flooding
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Remove the ping endpoint if it is not essential for the application's functionality. 2. Implement rate limiting on the ping endpoint to restrict the number of requests per user. 3. Use asynchronous processing for network operations to avoid blocking the application. 4. Log and monitor ping requests to detect and block abusive behavior.

vulnerabilities.title: Brute Force Login Attacks Leading to Account Lockout
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Implement account lockout policies that temporarily lock accounts after a threshold of failed attempts but unlock them after a short period. 2. Use CAPTCHA or multi-factor authentication (MFA) to prevent automated brute force attacks. 3. Enforce strong password policies to reduce the likelihood of successful brute force attacks. 4. Monitor and log login attempts to detect and block suspicious activity.

vulnerabilities.title: Regex-Based DoS via Search Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Avoid using complex regex patterns in user-facing input processing. 2. Use timeouts for regex processing to limit CPU usage. 3. Sanitize and validate user input before processing it with regex. 4. Use alternative string matching methods where possible (e.g., exact matching or simple wildcards).

vulnerabilities.title: Memory Exhaustion via Session Storage
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Use server-side session storage with a scalable backend (e.g., Redis or database-backed sessions). 2. Implement session expiration and cleanup policies to remove stale sessions. 3. Limit the number of active sessions per user. 4. Monitor memory usage and set alerts for abnormal spikes.

vulnerabilities.title: DoS via Profile Endpoint Data Processing
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Implement rate limiting on the profile endpoint to restrict the number of requests per user. 2. Compress or resize large data (e.g., images) before processing or storing them. 3. Use pagination for large datasets to limit the amount of data returned per request. 4. Cache frequently accessed profile data to reduce server load.

vulnerabilities.title: Network Amplification via Download Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: 1. Restrict the download endpoint to serve only pre-approved files or files stored within the application. 2. Implement rate limiting on the download endpoint. 3. Use content delivery networks (CDNs) to offload file downloads. 4. Validate and sanitize user input to prevent requests for external or unauthorized files.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in User Profile Access
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement proper authorization checks to ensure users can only access their own profiles. Use indirect references (e.g., UUIDs or session-based tokens) instead of predictable identifiers like sequential integers. Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) for sensitive operations.

vulnerabilities.title: Privilege Escalation via Weak Session Management
vulnerabilities.fix: Use strong, randomly generated session tokens (e.g., UUIDv4 or JWT with strong secrets). Implement session expiration, secure cookie attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), and proper session invalidation on logout. Consider using frameworks like Flask-Session or Flask-Login with built-in security features.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection Leading to Privilege Escalation
vulnerabilities.fix: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., SQLAlchemy ORM or Flask-SQLAlchemy) to prevent SQL injection. Avoid raw SQL queries with user input. Implement input validation and use least-privilege database accounts.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization Checks in Admin Endpoints
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement strict role-based access control (RBAC) for all admin endpoints. Use decorators or middleware (e.g., Flask's `@roles_required`) to enforce authorization. Regularly audit endpoints for missing checks.

vulnerabilities.title: Privilege Escalation via Mass Assignment
vulnerabilities.fix: Use explicit allowlists to define which fields users can update. Avoid binding user input directly to database models. Implement server-side validation to reject unauthorized field modifications.

vulnerabilities.title: Exploitation of Over-Permissive CORS Policies
vulnerabilities.fix: Restrict CORS policies to trusted domains only. Avoid using wildcards (`*`) for sensitive endpoints. Implement CSRF tokens for state-changing operations and validate the `Origin` header.

vulnerabilities.title: Privilege Escalation via Insecure File Uploads
vulnerabilities.fix: Restrict file uploads to allowed types (e.g., CSV, JSON) and validate file contents. Store uploaded files outside the web root and use random filenames. Disable execution permissions for uploaded files and scan them for malware.

vulnerabilities.title: Exploitation of Debug Mode in Production
vulnerabilities.fix: Disable debug mode in production (`app.run(debug=False)`). Use environment variables to manage configuration and ensure sensitive data (e.g., secrets) is not exposed in error messages or logs.

vulnerabilities.title: Privilege Escalation via Insecure Deserialization
vulnerabilities.fix: Avoid deserializing user-controlled data. Use safe serialization formats (e.g., JSON) and validate all inputs. If deserialization is necessary, use digital signatures or encryption to ensure data integrity.

vulnerabilities.title: Exploitation of Default or Weak Credentials
vulnerabilities.fix: Enforce strong password policies (e.g., minimum length, complexity) and disable default accounts. Implement account lockout after failed attempts and use multi-factor authentication (MFA) for admin accounts. Regularly audit credentials for weakness.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection in User Login and Profile Endpoints
vulnerabilities.fix: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) to separate SQL logic from user-supplied data. Avoid dynamic SQL construction with user input.
remediation_steps: Replace dynamic SQL queries with parameterized queries using `sqlite3` placeholders (`?`).
Use an ORM (e.g., SQLAlchemy) to abstract database interactions.
Implement input validation to reject malicious characters (e.g., quotes, semicolons).
Apply the principle of least privilege to the database user (e.g., read-only access where possible).

vulnerabilities.title: OS Command Injection in Ping Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Avoid using user input in shell commands. Use safe APIs or libraries to interact with system functions.
remediation_steps: Replace `subprocess.check_output` with a safe alternative (e.g., `subprocess.run` with a hardcoded command and a list of arguments).
If user input is required, validate and sanitize it strictly (e.g., allow only alphanumeric characters and dots).
Use a allowlist of allowed hosts or IP addresses.
Run the application with minimal privileges (e.g., non-root user).

vulnerabilities.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
vulnerabilities.fix: Replace hard-coded credentials with environment variables or a secure secrets management system.
remediation_steps: Store secrets (e.g., `SECRET_KEY`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `API_KEY`) in environment variables or a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).
Use a secure random generator to create secrets (e.g., `secrets.token_hex(32)` for `SECRET_KEY`).
Rotate all hard-coded credentials immediately after deployment.
Restrict access to the source code and use tools to scan for hard-coded secrets (e.g., GitGuardian, TruffleHog).

vulnerabilities.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Search Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Sanitize and escape all user-supplied input before reflecting it in HTML responses. Use templating engines that auto-escape by default.
remediation_steps: Use Flask's `escape` function to sanitize user input (e.g., `from markupsafe import escape`).
Use a templating engine like Jinja2, which auto-escapes variables by default.
Implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) to mitigate the impact of XSS.
Validate user input to reject scripts or HTML tags.

vulnerabilities.title: Path Traversal in Download Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Validate and sanitize user-supplied file paths. Use allowlists to restrict access to specific files or directories.
remediation_steps: Use `os.path.basename` to extract the filename and reject paths containing `..` or `/`.
Implement an allowlist of allowed filenames.
Use `os.path.abspath` to resolve the path and verify it is within the intended directory.
Store files outside the web root and serve them via a secure API.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Deserialization in Import Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Avoid deserializing untrusted data. Use safe serialization formats (e.g., JSON) and validate all inputs.
remediation_steps: Replace `pickle` with a safe serialization format like JSON (`json.loads`).
If `pickle` is required, use digital signatures to verify the integrity of serialized data before deserialization.
Implement strict input validation to reject malformed or unexpected data.
Run the application with minimal privileges to limit the impact of code execution.

vulnerabilities.title: Use of Broken Cryptographic Algorithm (MD5) for Password Hashing
vulnerabilities.fix: Replace MD5 with a modern, slow hashing algorithm designed for passwords (e.g., Argon2, bcrypt, or PBKDF2).
remediation_steps: Use `werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash` (which uses PBKDF2 by default) to hash passwords.
Enforce strong password policies (e.g., minimum length, complexity).
Salt all passwords to prevent rainbow table attacks.
Rotate all existing MD5-hashed passwords after upgrading the hashing algorithm.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Profile Endpoint
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement proper authorization checks to ensure users can only access their own data or data they are authorized to view.
remediation_steps: Verify that the requesting user is authorized to access the requested profile (e.g., check session data).
Use indirect references (e.g., UUIDs or session-based identifiers) instead of direct object references.
Implement role-based access control (RBAC) to restrict access to sensitive data.
Log and monitor access to sensitive endpoints.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Security Headers and Debug Mode Enabled
vulnerabilities.fix: Disable debug mode in production and implement security headers to mitigate common web vulnerabilities.
remediation_steps: Set `debug=False` in production.
Add security headers to all HTTP responses (e.g., CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options).
Use Flask-Talisman to enforce HTTPS and security headers.
Regularly audit security configurations using tools like OWASP ZAP or Burp Suite.
